diagnoses.name: Possible Meconium Aspiration
diagnoses.text1:
Think - is this really Meconium aspiration?
Just because there was meconium at delivery doesn't mean it was aspirated! 
Most aspiration occurs in utero before the baby is born, so more likely if there was foetal distress

Babies with mec aspiration are sick with significant respiratory distress and may have signs of birth asphyxia. Floppy babies with severe HIE and Meconium aspiration are unlikely to benefit from CPAP. 

1. Airway and respiratory support 

- Position airway & suction
- If sats < 90% in air put on oxygen
- If > 1kg consider CPAP according to TRY-CPAP algorithm
diagnoses.text2:
2. Feeding support 

- If breathing 60-80 bpm use cup/NGT
- If needing CPAP use OGT
- If breathing > 80 bpm consider IV fluids
diagnoses.text3:
3. IV Access for antibiotics 

Give antibiotics

symptoms.name: History of fast or laboured breathing
Any severity of work of breathing

diagnoses.name: Suspected neonatal sepsis
diagnoses.expressionMeaning: Sepsis table score; 1 factor or more has been selected
diagnoses.text1:
1.	Perform cultures BEFORE giving antibiotics if possible
Follow the unit blood culture taking guidelines, with special care to minimise contamination and ensure an adequate blood volume in the bottle (1-2 ml). 

If it is impossible to perform the culture, antibiotics should not be delayed, but this is sub-optimal medicine. 
If the suspicion of meningitis is strong, one should perform a lumbar puncture before starting antibiotics if possible.
diagnoses.text2:
2. Antibiotics 

Start antibiotics:
- Penicillin 50,000 IU/kg 12 hourly IV/IM and 
- Gentamicin 
Low birth weight (<2500g) - 3mg/kg 24 hourly IV or IM 
Normal birth weight (>2500g) - 5mg/kg 24 hourly IV or IM

Change frequency of Penicillin to 6 hourly if > 7days age
Change dose of Gentamicin to 7.5mg/kg every 24 hours if > 7 days age

Length of antibiotics: 
Stop at five days if baby well and all investigations are negative
If blood culture comes back negative before 5 days and baby is well then stop antibiotics when negative culture result received. 
If clinically unwell, give 7-10 days, though meningitis or suspected bone/joint infections require longer

Give 14-21 days with high suspicion of meningitis or positive CSF culture result
 
If GBS positive CSF result treat for 14 days
If E.coli or Klebsiella give 21 days
diagnoses.text3:
3. Supportive care 
Check blood sugar and provide feeding support if needed
 
Give 2.0 mL/kg 10% dextrose bolus if blood glucose <2.6 and baby symptomatic
 
Give 10mL/kg fluid bolus if shocked
 
Thermoregulation: aim for body temperature between 36.5 - 37.5
 
If baby has fever (T = 38.5) remove from warmer and unwrap 
 
Provide respiratory support as needed

diagnoses.name: Difficulty Feeding
diagnoses.text1:
Baby stable breathing <60bpm

If baby cannot feed adequately by breast or bottle but is stable, try using a cup or spoon
diagnoses.text2:
Tachypnoea, breathing > 60bpm

If baby is breathing fast, tired or struggling to feed, insert a naso/orogastric tube and give feeds down the tube via syringe every 2 hours
diagnoses.text3:
Tachypnoea, breathing > 80bpm 

If baby is in significant distress, breathing over 80 times/minute or exhibiting other danger signs, stop feeds and begin IV fluids.

diagnoses.name: Dehydration
diagnoses.text1: Refer to WHO plan A, B or C as below:

diagnoses.name: Congenital Heart Disease
diagnoses.text1: 1. Keep warm and closely monitor baby
diagnoses.text2:
2. Respiratory support 

If duct dependent heart disease suspected try not to over oxygenate
Discuss with physician
diagnoses.text3:
3. Feeding support 

Use naso/Oro gastric feeding to reduce WOB


Refer for echocardiogram 
- Try to get a CXR and Echo locally 
- Send FBC, Group and cross match
- Assess for signs of heart failure - consider diuretics 
- Refer to paediatric cardiologist in tertiary centre if possible

diagnoses.name: Anaemia
diagnoses.text1:
1. Limit blood loss and supportive care
- Stop any active bleeding
- Keep warm
- Support feeding
diagnoses.text2:
2. Send FBC, Group and cross match
- Evaluate causes
diagnoses.text3:
3. Consider blood transfusion if...
- Severe anaemia - paper white appearance
- Associated respiratory distress
- Signs of heart failure
- Hb less than ....

diagnoses.name: Congenital Abnormality
diagnoses.text1:
Congenital abnormality Includes:
- Neural tube defect 
- Abdominal wall defect 
- Cleft palate
diagnoses.text2:
Refer to surgeons 
Specifically refer to orthopaedics for bone injuries or abnormalities 

Treat for sepsis / risk of sepsis 
If there is any fever 38.0 or more treat with antibiotics 
NTDs are high risk for sepsis and meningitis
Prophylactic antibiotics may be appropriate
diagnoses.text3:
Counselling 

Discuss sensitively how antenatal folate treatment can prevent another neural tube defect in subsequent pregnancies.

Postition airway & suction
If sats < 90% in air put on oxygen
If > 1 kg consider CPAP according to TRY algorithm
diagnoses.text2:
2. Feeding support
If breathing 60-80 bpm use cup/NGT
If needing CPAP use OGT
If breathing > 80bpm consider IV fluids
diagnoses.text3:

Before commencing antibiotics consider sepsis screen

diagnoses.name: Transient Tachypnoea of Newborn (TTN)
diagnoses.text1:
These babies are not unwell 
RR is usually between 60-80 breaths per minute & don't need oxygen
This should resolve in 6 hours!
TTN is more likely following elective C-section due to wet lungs
diagnoses.text2:
1. Airway and respiratory support
- Position airway in neutral and suction if necessary
- If sats < 90% in air put on oxygen - diagnosis is unlikely TTN! 

2. Feeding support
- Babies with TTN are likely to need cup/NGT until RR < 60
diagnoses.text3:
3. Antibiotics are not needed!

If the Tachypnoea continues longer than 6 hours or any other signs/symptoms develop e.g. fever then it is unlikely TTN and might be sepsis so start antibiotics.

diagnoses.name: Convulsions
diagnoses.expressionMeaning: Convulsions seen on examination or history
diagnoses.text1:
Refer to management of convulsions flow chart on wall

1. Airway management & oxygen
- Neutral position
- Check for secretions, suction if needed 
- Put on oxygen
diagnoses.text2:
2. Check blood glucose
- If < 45 mg/dl or < 2.5 mmol/L give IV 10% glucose at 2ml/kg
- If blood glucose monitoring not available give IV 10% glucose at 2ml/kg
- Do full infection screen
- If possible take blood for Ca, Mg, U and E’s, FBC
diagnoses.text3:
3. Give anticonvulsants
- Give phenobarbitone 20mg/kg IM 
- Repeat loading dose if necessary
- If seizures ongoing give Paraldehyde Dose: 0.2 ml/kg IM, 0.4 ml/kg PR 
- If seizures still ongoing - give maintenance phenobarbitone 5mg/kg PO/IM

When seizures have stopped and baby stable click the blue arrow to continue

diagnoses.name: Low Birth Weight (1500-2499g)

1800-2500g: 
- These babies are usually strong enough to feed normally on the breast after birth
diagnoses.text2:

- If the baby is not feeding well by breast, bottle, or cup or exhibiting any danger signs the baby should stay in special care nursery

- Needs admission to special care nursery for close observation

diagnoses.name: Mild Hypothermia
diagnoses.expressionMeaning: Baby's temperature is recorded as 36 degrees up to 36.4 degrees
diagnoses.text1:
1) Warm the baby 
Skin to skin (KMC position) or place on warmer or resuscitaire
diagnoses.text2:
2) Limit heat loss 
- Make sure baby is dry 
- Put on a hat & wrap up the baby  
- If on the resuscitaire put the sides up 
- (consider) The 4 ways by which a baby may lose heat are:
diagnoses.text3:
3) Monitor temperature 
- Check temperature every 15-30 mins or until warm between 36.6-37.5'C
- Watch out for over-warming (>37.5)
- Complete the Neotree assessment to assess for signs of infection, apnoea and hypoglycaemia

diagnoses.name: Premature (32-36 weeks)
diagnoses.expressionMeaning: Baby's gestation is 32 weeks to 36 weeks
diagnoses.text1:
1. Thermoregulation 

If needing oxygen  
- for babies < 1800 g use radiant warmer + intermittent KMC
- for babies > 1800 g radiant warmer

If not needing oxygen 
- for babies < 1800g KMC
- for babies 1800 - 2500 ambulatory KMC 

Remember to perform Ballard Score- images are for neuromuscular followed by physical maturity assessment  - (Ballad score images in script)
diagnoses.text2:
2. Respiratory support

Oxygen / CPAP
CPAP >28 weeks or > 1000g and passes the TRY CPAP algorithm (image in script)
Remember preterms may have slightly reduced tone due to their prematurity
Early CPAP for babies between 28 - 32 weeks
Give aminophylline (or caffeine if available) to prevent apnoeas
diagnoses.text3:
3. Feeding support 

If able to suck can breast feed 

If not able to suck give cup feeds or consider OGT 
OGT for all babies < 1500g, RR > 60 and needing respiratory support
OGT if on CPAP
Consider IV fluids in smaller babies breathing > 80 bpm

diagnoses.name: Hypoglycaemia (symptomatic)
diagnoses.expressionMeaning: Blood sugar below 2.5mmol and showing symptoms
diagnoses.text1:
Do the following and refer to page 311 COIN, Chart C

1. Give dextrose bolus 
- 2ml/kg of 10% dextrose IV over 5 minutes
- If no IV line, give the same IV dextrose by gastric tube.
diagnoses.text2:
2. Give Maintenance fluids 

For fluid and rate see Wall Chart
diagnoses.text3:
3. Monitor Blood Glucose after 30 minutes 

For further management refer to the wall chart

diagnoses.name: Hypoglycaemia (NOT symptomatic)
diagnoses.expressionMeaning: Blood sugar below 2.5mmol and NOT showing symptoms
diagnoses.text1:
Do the following & refer to page 310 COIN, chart B 

1. Continue Breast Feeding or giving EBM by cup
diagnoses.text2: 2. Increase frequency of feeds e.g. from 3 to 2 hourly or from 2 to 1 hourly
diagnoses.text3:
3. Monitor blood glucose before next feed or immediately if any symptoms!

For further management refer to the wall chart

diagnoses.name: At Risk of Hypoglycaemia
diagnoses.expressionMeaning:
Birth weight less than 2500g or greater than 4000g
Gestation less than 37wks
Mother has diabetes or received steroids
Baby admitted for Neonatal Encephalopathy
diagnoses.text1:
A baby presenting with any of the following conditions listed below is at risk of hypoglycaemia:
-	Birth weight <2500g
-	Birth weight >4000g
-	Infants of diabetic mothers
-	Preterm <37 weeks 
-	Maternal beta blocker use
-	Perinatal asphyxia, HIE, Neonatal encephalopathy
-	Late preterm exposure to antenatal steroids
diagnoses.text2:
Monitor blood sugars:
-	Ensure that baby is offered the breast within the first 60 minutes
-	Check blood glucose before the second feed (2-4 hours after birth)
-	If 3 normal blood sugars (>2.5 – 8.3mmol) on postnatal ward or NNU monitoring can be stopped
-	If blood sugar <2.5mmol (or < 45mgdL) follow the hypoglycaemia management pathway

diagnoses.name: HIV Unknown
diagnoses.expressionMeaning: Unknown HIV status or HIV test results
diagnoses.text1:
This mother and baby need an URGENT HIV test
Rapid HIV test needed and treat as high risk if reactive
diagnoses.text2:
A high risk infant is born to a mother who:
1.	Had a viral load >1000 copies/mL in the 4 weeks before delivery OR
2.	Received <4 weeks of ART at delivery OR
3.	Was newly diagnosed with HIV during labour, delivery or post partum

Infants should receive: 
NVP for 12 weeks if breast fed
NVP for 6 weeks if formula fed
Infants should have a DNA PCR as soon as possible after delivery and again at 6 weeks if birth PCR negative. Serology should be tested at 9 and 18 months. 

Dose as per table
diagnoses.text3:
If < 2kg: (as per WHO guidelines)
NVP 2mg/kg per day to 2 weeks 
        4mg/kg per day 2-6 weeks

diagnoses.name: HIV Low Risk
diagnoses.expression: ($MatHIVtest = true) and ($HIVtestResult = 'R' or $HIVtestResult = 'U') and ($LengthHAART = '1stTrim' or $LengthHAART = '2ndTrim' or $LengthHAART = '3rdTrim')
diagnoses.expressionMeaning:
HIV test is reactive/ unknown
HAART received within trimesters 1-3
diagnoses.text1: The baby is LOW RISK
diagnoses.text2:
- These infants are born to women established on ART with viral suppression <1000 copies/mL or more than 4 weeks of ART
- They should receive daily NVP for 6 weeks 

ALL HIV EXPOSED BABIES SHOULD RECEIVE A DNA PCR AT BIRTH REGARDLESS OF HIGH/LOW RISK

- DNA PCR should be tested  again at 6 weeks, and serology at 9 and 18 months. 
DNA PCR test: If DNA PCR test positive, commence full ART as soon as possible

Dose as per table

diagnoses.name: Physiological Jaundice
diagnoses.expressionMeaning: The baby has physiological jaundice which is characterised by yellow eyes and skin and no signs of pathological jaundice.
diagnoses.text1:
1. Take Transcutaneous Bilirubin (TCB) measurement

Take a TCB measurement from the forehead, sternum and abdomen and plot the highest of these 3 measurements
diagnoses.text2: 2. Encourage and support breastfeeding
diagnoses.text3: 3. Educate parents on how to monitor for jaundice

diagnoses.name: Pathological Jaundice
diagnoses.expression: ($YColour = 'Y' and $Age < 24) or ($YColour = 'Y' and $Age > 23.9 and (($Age < 336 and $Gestation > 36.6) or ($Age < 504 and $Gestation < 37)) and ($Jaundice = 'DJ' or $Temperature > 37 or $BirthWeight < 2500 or $Colour = 'White'))
diagnoses.expressionMeaning: Deep jaundice (yellow palms and soles)Prematurity (<35 weeks or < 2.5 kg)
diagnoses.text1:
1. Start phototherapy immediately

Take transcutaneous bilirubin and send serum bilirubin and plot
Send full blood count, blood group (mother and baby) and syphilis serology. Perform coombs test and glucose 6-phosphate deficiency if available. 
Always consider and treat for infection and perform Thompson score to assess for encephalopathy
Start phototherapy
diagnoses.text2:
2. Whilst on phototherapy 

Repeat transcutaneous bilirubin every 24 hours/once a day after starting or stopping and plot trend. 
Give eye protection for baby
Undress to nappy
Maintain normothermia
Encourage and support breast feeding 
Assess for signs of dehydration: Give 20 mL/kg top up with cup EBM or OGT if necessary
Send serum bilirubin if clinically deteriorating 
If bilirubin rises above exchange transfusion line, perform exchange transfusion if safe and possible to do so
diagnoses.text3:
3. When to stop phototherapy

Stop phototherapy if bilirubin is under the treatment threshold range or no jaundice of palms and soles

diagnoses.name: Prolonged Jaundice
diagnoses.expressionMeaning: Prolonged jaundice > 14 days term or >21 days preterm infants
diagnoses.text1:
1. Needs further investigation to exclude:

Liver/metabolic disorder – Perform liver function tests and calculate percentage of conjugated to 
unconjugated bilirubin (if more than 20% it is conjugated hyperbilirubinemia)
Hypothyroidism  - perform thyroid function tests if available
Biliary atresia  - perform abdominal USS if conjugated hyperbilirubinemia and pale stools
diagnoses.text2: 2. Encourage and support breast feeding

diagnoses.name: Hypoxic Ischaemic Encephalopathy
diagnoses.text1:
1. Supportive care:

ABCD
Prevent hyperthermia
Start feeds to MAXIMUM of 40ml/kg/day
Observe for 72 hours
diagnoses.text2:
2. If the baby has seizures

Check glucose and treat abnormal glucose
Load with phenobarbitone (20mg/kg IM)
If ongoing seizures, repeat loading dose of phenobarbitone and start maintenance
diagnoses.text3:
3. Reassess TS 8 hourly. 

Normal neurology, no convulsions. At 72 hours.
Stop phenobarbitone


Abnormal neurology/ convulsions. At 72 hours.
Discuss with senior paediatrician

diagnoses.name: Prematurity with Respiratory Distress
diagnoses.expression: $Gestation < 37 and ($RR > 60 or $DangerSigns = 'Grun' or $DangerSigns = 'Cyan' or $SatsAIr < 90 or $SatsO2 < 90 or $RespSR = 'DIB' or $RespSR = 'BE' or $RespSR = 'Apn' or $RespSR = 'Cough' or $RespSR = 'NBr' or $SignsRD = 'TT' or $SignsRD = 'NFL' or $SignsRD = 'CHI' or $SignsRD = 'HN' or $SignsRD = 'ST' or $SignsRD = 'GR' or $SignsRD = 'Gasp' or $SignsRD = 'GR')
diagnoses.text1:
Care must be given to thermoregulation as per preterm guidelines
Remember to perform Ballard Score- images are first Neuromuscular followed by Physical maturity assessment

1. Airway and Respiratory support 
Position the airway in neutral
If saturations < 90% put on oxygen
If distress is significant & > 1kg consider CPAP according to the TRY CPAP algorithm.
Start on Aminophylline if baby is < 34 week or <1.5kg 
Consider surfactant if >1000g with severe respiratory distress requiring CPAP and an oxygen requirement >35%
diagnoses.text2:
2. Feeding support 

If breathing 60-80 bpm use cup/OGT
If needing CPAP use OGT
If breathing > 80 bpm consider IV fluids
diagnoses.text3:
3. Get IV access and start antibiotics 

Antibiotics are recommended in all preterms with RDS if mother confirmed sepsis or suspected chorioamnionitis OR spontaneous preterm labour OR with 2 or more of the following risk factors for sepsis 

Risk factors:

Take blood culture (if possible) before starting antibiotics 
Obtain IV access & commence 
- Penicillin 50,000 IU/kg 12 hourly IV/IM and
- Gentamicin 
Low birth weight (<2500g) - 3mg/kg 24 hourly IV or IM 
Normal birth weight (>2500g) - 5mg/kg 24 hourly IV or IM

For senior doctor review for duration of antibiotics

symptoms.name: History of fast or laboured breathing

diagnoses.name: Term baby with Respiratory Distress
diagnoses.expression: $Gestation >= 37 and ($RR > 60 or $DangerSigns = 'Grun' or $DangerSigns = 'Cyan' or $SatsAIr < 90 or $SatsO2 < 90 or $RespSR = 'DIB' or $RespSR = 'BE' or $RespSR = 'Apn' or $RespSR = 'Cough' or $RespSR = 'NBr' or $SignsRD = 'TT' or $SignsRD = 'HN' or $SignsRD = 'ST' or $SignsRD = 'NFL' or $SignsRD = 'CHI' or $SignsRD = 'GR' or $SignsRD = 'Gasp' or $SignsRD = 'GR')
diagnoses.expressionMeaning: Baby is term and showed one of the signs/risks of respiratory distress.
diagnoses.text1:
1. Airway and Breathing

Position airway in neutral 
Apply nasal prong oxygen to maintain saturations 90-95%
Consider CPAP as per TRY CPAP algorithm  if > 1kg and good tone but if the RR>60, Room oxygen saturations are < 90% or if there are retractions and grunting per flowchart below.
diagnoses.text2:
2. Feeding support:

If >34 weeks or >1500g and NOT on CPAP use cup/OGT feeding until RR <60 bpm
OGT for all babies < 1500g, RR > 60 and needing respiratory support
OGT if on CPAP
Consider IV fluids if respiratory rate > 80 bpm
diagnoses.text3:
3. Antibiotics:  - If respiratory distress started greater than 4 hours old (if there are no other conditions requiring antibiotics earlier than 4 hours old) and ongoing respiratory distress:

Take blood culture before starting antibiotics 
Obtain IV access & commence 
- Penicillin 50,000 IU/kg 12 hourly IV/IM and
- Gentamicin 
Low birth weight (<2500g) - 3mg/kg 24 hourly IV or IM 
Normal birth weight (>2500g) - 5mg/kg 24 hourly IV or IM

4. Meconium

Most meconium aspiration occurs in utero before the baby is born, so more likely if there was foetal distress
Suspect meconium aspiration IF sick with significant respiratory distress +/- signs of birth asphyxia and consider starting this baby on antibiotics
Floppy babies with severe HIE and Meconium aspiration are unlikely to benefit from CPAP

diagnoses.name: Gastroschisis
diagnoses.text1:
1. Surgical assessment 

Primary repair is considered on day 1 if infant is less than 6 hours old and all bowel is viable.
If there are signs of sepsis or non-viable bowel (conduct PILO SCORE) then surgeons apply a silo bag
If it’s viable and <6 hrs the surgeons do primary repair on day 1. If there are signs of sepsis or distended bowels, then you add a bag.

diagnoses.text1:
1. Handle with sterile, latex-free gloves (if possible) and sterile towels at delivery

Nurse side-lying or prone to ensure no pressure is placed on the lesion
Wrap lesion with sterile gauze soaked in warm saline
diagnoses.text2:
2. Antibiotics

Apply topical tetracycline and give IV Benzylpenicillin (100-150 mg/kg daily in two divided doses) or Ampicillin (25-50 mg/kg IM or IV four times a day) PLUS Amikacin for 5 days

Refer to Paediatric Neurosurgeon for closure.
diagnoses.text3:
3. Monitoring

Monitor daily head circumference  and obtain Cranial USS and CT (if CrUSS is of concern and possible) 
Monitor for symptoms of bowel, bladder and motor deficit and hydrocephalus (apnoea, bradycardia, hypoventilation, stridor, swallow dysfunction) 

Monitor urine output and obtain renal ultrasound (if possible). Check Creatine Day 5 to 7

From the information entered so far this baby is one who can be exclusively breastfed
Breastmilk is the ideal food for most babies and has a huge number of benefits
managementMetadata.title: Exclusively Breastfeed
managementMetadata.title2: Some babies may need extra support
managementMetadata.text1:
Aim to feed within the first hour of life
Offer feeding at regular intervals or in response to signals from baby
Do not leave longer than 3 hours between offering feeds
Give mother advice on positioning and attachment of the baby
If baby is struggling to breastfeed then skin to skin contact with mother and regularly offering the breast can be helpful if baby is well
managementMetadata.text2:
Small babies or babies who are unwell may need extra support
Offer cup feeds to top up breastfeeds if needed
Use volumes as per COIN guidance 
If a baby is struggling with cup or breastfeeding they may need an NG or OG tube.
managementMetadata.text3:
If mother is not available then discuss options with senior clinicians
Ideally babies should receive donor breast milk where available
